laws.rule: Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis Act, RSA 2000, c. G-1, s. 90.28: nobody may smoke or vape cannabis where smoking is banned under the Tobacco, Smoking and Vaping Reduction Act, another Act or a municipal bylaw; on hospital, school or child care property; or in or within a set distance of a playground, sports field, skateboard or bicycle park, zoo, outdoor theatre, or outdoor pool or splash pad. The distances are in regulations not read here. Cannabis may not be used in a vehicle unless the vehicle is a temporary residence at the time (s. 90.24). Cannabis in a vehicle must be in closed packaging out of reach of the driver and other occupants (s. 90.25). A minor (under 18) may not buy, obtain or possess cannabis (s. 90.26).

The legal drinking age in Alberta is 18: a minor (under 18) may not buy, obtain, possess or drink liquor, and nobody may sell or give liquor to a minor, except that a parent, guardian or spouse may give liquor to a minor in a residence or temporary residence (Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis Act, s. 87).

Nobody may drink liquor in a public place, or anywhere other than a residence, temporary residence (such as a camper or motor home), licensed premises or a place prescribed in regulations (s. 89(1)). Exceptions: a public-park picnic area the park owner has designated, with a sign stating the area and hours (s. 89(2)); and a municipal entertainment district designated by bylaw (s. 89(4)). A police officer can order someone to stop drinking in a designated picnic area if they appear intoxicated (s. 89(3)). Nobody may drink liquor in a vehicle unless it is a temporary residence at the time (s. 84).

Tobacco, Smoking and Vaping Reduction Act, s. 3: smoking and vaping are banned on hospital, child care and school property (including parking areas), in workplaces, in public places (which includes patios and pools), in public vehicles such as buses and taxis, and in any vehicle with a minor in it. They are also banned in or within a set distance of playgrounds, sports fields, skateboard and bicycle parks, zoos, outdoor theatres and public outdoor pools, and within a set distance of the doors, windows and air intakes of the indoor places listed. Distances are set in regulations not read here.

items.text: The legal age for cannabis in Alberta is 18 (most of Canada is 19). Adults may carry up to 30 g of dried cannabis (or equivalent) in public, and buy only from private licensed stores, in person or online.

No one may use cannabis in a vehicle unless the vehicle is being used as a temporary residence at the time. Cannabis carried in a vehicle must be in closed packaging, out of reach of the driver and passengers (Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis Act, s. 90.24 and 90.25).

You can't smoke or vape cannabis anywhere tobacco smoking is banned, on hospital, school or child care grounds, or within a set distance of places such as playgrounds, zoos, outdoor pools and splash pads (s. 90.28).

The legal drinking age is 18: the Act defines a minor as a person under 18, and a minor can't buy, obtain, possess or drink liquor (s. 87). Adults may drink in a residence, a temporary residence, licensed premises or another place the regulations allow; drinking in other public places is banned (s. 86(5), 89(1)). A park owner or operator can designate a picnic area where drinking is allowed during set hours, if signs say so (s. 89(2)).

Alberta licenses psychedelic drug treatment services (therapy using a designated psychedelic drug) under the Mental Health Services Protection Act and its Regulation. Providers need a provincial licence unless exempt (approved clinical trials, and ketamine used outside psychedelic-assisted psychotherapy), must meet the Psychedelic Drug Treatment Services Standards, and have clinical oversight by a psychiatrist. A provincial licence sits alongside the federal rules on possession; it doesn't replace them.

layers.process: Moraine Lake Road is closed to personal vehicles year-round. Only Parks Canada shuttles, licensed commercial operators with a Moraine Lake Road Licence of Occupation, and registered guests of Moraine Lake Lodge may use it. Parks Canada says Roam Public Transit and Parks Canada shuttles are the easiest ways to reach the lakes. Parks Canada shuttles need a reservation (Parks Canada Reservation Service online, or 1-877-737-3783). For 2026, 40% of seats were released on 15 April and the rest are released at 8 am Mountain time two days before each departure day. One ticket covers Lake Louise Lakeshore, Moraine Lake, the Lake Connector and the return to the Lake Louise Park and Ride, where free parking is available to reservation holders and check-in is required in the one-hour departure window. 2026 seasons: Lake Louise Lakeshore 15 May to 12 October; Moraine Lake, Lake Connector and Alpine Start (4 am and 5 am departures from the Lakeshore car park) 1 June to 12 October, weather permitting. Those 2026 dates have ended; the 2027 season was not published on the page read. The shuttle ticket does not include the national park pass. Moraine Lake has no cell service, Wi-Fi or running water; pit toilets only. A personal vehicle can still go to Lake Louise Lakeshore (payment required May to October), but Parks Canada says parking there is unlikely to be found. Accessible shuttles run on demand if you tell staff at check-in (not on Alpine Start in 2026).

Shuttle fares (Parks Canada Shuttle, Lake Louise, Moraine Lake and Alpine Start): adult C$12.75 (about A$13), senior C$6.00 (about A$6), youth 17 and under C$4.00 (about A$4), plus a non-refundable reservation fee of C$3.50 online or C$5.50 by phone (changes or cancellations cost the same fee again). Parking at Lake Louise Lakeshore is C$42.00 per vehicle (about A$43) from 15 May to 12 October 2026. Rate: A$1 = CAD 0.9838 (RBA, 30 Oct 2026), so C$1 is about A$1.02.

layers.authority: Parks Canada, Banff, Jasper, Kootenay, Yoho and other national parks
layers.process: A national park pass is required for anyone spending time in Banff National Park, including on the Icefields Parkway (#93N) and Bow Valley Parkway (#1A); you do not need one if you only drive through without stopping, except on those parkways. The same daily pass works in Banff, Jasper, Kootenay, Yoho, Mount Revelstoke, Glacier, Waterton Lakes and Elk Island. Banff's and Jasper's fee pages list: daily adult C$12.25 (about A$12.45), senior C$10.75 (about A$10.95), family or group up to seven people in one vehicle C$24.50 (about A$24.90), youth 17 and under free; annual Discovery Pass adult C$83.50 (about A$84.90), senior C$71.50, family or group C$167.50. A daily pass is valid until 4 pm the day after purchase. Both fee pages said on 6 November 2026 that the Parks Canada passes and permits sales page was having technical difficulties and pass orders were unavailable online; daily passes can be bought at park gates and information centres. Rate: A$1 = CAD 0.9838 (RBA, 30 Oct 2026).
